newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - KNP BT Q1 results seen bleak.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - KNP BT Q1 results seen bleak.

text.p: Dutch paper, packaging and office equipment group NV Koninklijke KNP BT is expected to post another profit fall for the first quarter of 1997 on Friday due to its ailing paper division, analysts expect.
Forecasts for first quarter net profit from ordinary operations ranged from 40 to 48 million guilders, compared with 50 million in the first quarter of 1996.

KNP BT said in March first quarter profits would probably slightly lower than in 1996 due to disappointing business in the first two months of this year. It maintained its full-year prognosis that earnings from ordinary operations would improve.
But analysts said the paper sector was still suffering from a large overcapacity which put pressure on prices and margins.
Last week's results from Swedish competitor Stora, where 1997 first quarter profits plunged by 54 percent, showed little indication that this market was recovering, they added.

"At this moment I am still gambling on KNP BT compensating the first quarter drop to some extent in the rest of the year but if the (first quarter) figures or the outlook turn out to be disappointing I will cut my full-year forecast," said analyst Henk Brouwer of Bank Bangert Pontier.
Brouwer said many paper manufacturers, including KNP BT, had been too optimistic about a market recovery and had made things worse by building or expanding even more production units.
"They have clearly thought that the market would have recovered much more by now and kept gambling on that, and now that turns out to be quite a disappointment," he said.
In a recent analysts' report, ING Barings also pointed at new production capacity coming on stream in the second half of this year, which could dampen paper prices even more.
"A weaker demand could send prices back to early 1996 levels in the second half of 1997," ING Barings warned.
ING Barings also pointed to KNP BT's warning that first quarter profits would lag behind the 50 million guilders posted in 1996, and added that the year-ago figures were already unpromising.
Bangert Pontier's Brouwer said his firm had issued a Hold recommendation on KNP BT's stock in February but was now more inclined to cut this to a Sell.
"If the first quarter results are not much better than expected, I expect to cut it to a Sell, because it will not be a share then which offers many prospects," he said.
KNP BT previously said it would try to find a partner for its paper division but analysts said this might prove difficult given the present market conditions.
The production facilities of the company's Leykam division are modern and well up-to-date but in the present market situation, possible buyers would probably not be willing to pay a reasonable price.
"If a buyer just bases his price on the unit's profitability I think they (KNP BT) will get less for it than they have recently invested in it. Then it would be throwing away money," Brouwer said.

Although KNP BT said in February it would decide on the future of its paper division this year and said it was in talks with several parties, analysts do not expect the firm to come up with a partner soon.
"I would be very surprised if they could announce something at short notice," Bangert Pontier's Brouwer said.
